ink-faint.contrastNote: 4.54:1 vs paper (light), 5.56:1 vs paper (dark) — both clear WCAG AA 4.5:1 for text, verified 2026-09-04.

sealing-wax.contrastNote: 5.45:1 vs paper (light), 5.52:1 vs dark paper (dark) — verified 2026-09-04.

display.purpose: Every classification name and heading, always uppercase — the site brand, Explore row names, detail panel name, quiz question/result. The system's one loud gesture.

title.purpose: Section intros and the same oversized-uppercase treatment as display, at a slightly narrower size range for secondary headings.

body.purpose: Running prose — descriptions, taglines, hints — plus the rotated tab labels.

mono.purpose: Anything measured: indices, era dates, diagnostic labels, branch tags, footer credits, timeline marks. A number set in this face reads as data, not prose.

extensions.shadowNote: This system uses no box-shadow anywhere — see DESIGN.md's 'The Line, Not Light Rule'. Separation between surfaces comes from a 1px border (rule-solid for flush content, ink for floating panels) or a paper/panel tone shift, never blur.

motion.name: ease-cut
motion.purpose: Every state change (view fade-in, tooltip/popover appearance, row hover) steps rather than eases — an instant two-or-three-frame cut instead of a smooth curve, matching the system's printed/mechanical register. Replaces the previous world's soft opacity+translateY eases entirely.

breakpoints.name: tablet
breakpoints.purpose: Brand tagline switches from right-aligned to left-aligned and drops its max-width.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: Tab row gap tightens for small phones.

components.name: Tab

narrative.overview:
Type Classified reads as a technical reference, not a book: a page built like a measured drawing, where a dashed rule and a leader line prove a claim instead of decorating it. This replaced an earlier 'Specimen Ledger' identity (warm parchment, a serif display face, soft ambient shadows) at the user's explicit direction, pinned to two references — a portfolio built from massive stacked client names, and the Cooper Hewitt Museum's 'Type Culture Now' poster, with its dashed vertical grid and rotated section labels — translated onto a white ground instead of the originals' black.

Every classification name is set in a single oversized condensed grotesque, uppercase, carrying the page the way a poster's headline carries a spread. Everything measured — indices, era dates, diagnostic labels, dimension callouts — is set in a monospace, because a number in a monospace face reads as data, not prose. The one color note is a sealing-wax red, held to tags and measurement marks exactly as before; nothing else about the palette survived the replacement. Corners are square throughout and nothing casts a shadow — separation between surfaces comes from a rule line or a change in tone, never blur.
keyCharacteristics: Near-white ground, near-black ink — never a warm cream, never a soft shadow
One condensed display face (Anton) carries every name and headline, always uppercase
A monospace face marks anything measured: indices, dates, dimensions, tags
Dashed rules are structural, not decorative — they mark a grid, a leader line, a boundary
Square corners everywhere; separation comes from a rule or a tone change, never a shadow
The one accent color still marks only small things — tags, bars, measurement call-outs — never a fill

rules.name: The Small Mark Rule
rules.body: Sealing Wax never fills a surface larger than a tag, a 2px border, or a bar on the timeline. It marks; it never fills.

rules.name: The No-Warm-Neutral Rule
rules.body: No neutral in this system carries a warm parchment cast — paper, panel, ink, and rule are all genuinely near-white/near-black/near-gray. The previous identity's entire palette is the anti-reference here.

rules.name: The One Voice, One Data Rule
rules.body: Anton names things; Inter explains things; JetBrains Mono measures things. No role ever borrows another's job.

rules.name: The Line, Not Light Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow appears anywhere in this system. A surface separates from the page behind it with a border or a tone change; if neither reads clearly enough, the surface's content or size is wrong, not its shadow.

dos: Do set every classification name and heading in Anton, uppercase, at large scale.
Do set anything measured (an index, a date, a diagnostic, a dimension) in JetBrains Mono.
Do separate every surface with a border or a tone shift, never a shadow.
Do keep Sealing Wax to tags, bars, and measurement marks.
donts: Don't reintroduce a shadow anywhere, however soft.
Don't round a corner. border-radius: 0 is absolute, no exceptions — including SVG geometry.
Don't bring back a warm-toned neutral.

Don't ship a font whose classification lineage is wrong for the sake of a better-looking specimen — the live Aa Gg Qy specimens still render in each classification's own verified typeface beneath the new Anton display name, not replaced by it.
